messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep: BrightWorks account health & renewal risk register — exec attention

Team —

Quick heads-up ahead of this week’s QBR with BrightWorks (renewal window: Aug 15). I ran the health score and dug into the incident and support logs; key signals below that I want exec eyes on and a short list of asks. I’ll attach the working deck and the latest redlines we received from procurement.

Snapshot (TL;DR)
- ARR: $820k (renewal + potential 10% expansion).
- Health score: 63/100 (down 12 points QoQ). Main drivers: increased latency for long-context pipelines, two policy-related incidents in March, and lower-than-expected completion quality on a high-priority inference workload.
- Support noise: 18 tickets in last 90d; 3 Sev2s (one SLA breach for a scheduled migration).
- Risk signals: renewal negotiation started, buyer is pushing for 20% discount + performance remediation guarantees. Legal flagged one high-risk indemnity clause in their redlines.

Immediate asks (please respond by EOD Thu):
1) Exec attendance: We should have either Vivek or Laura represent product/ops at the customer QBR on 2027-06-02 10:00 PDT. Who can commit? (Vivek/Laura)
2) Credit/comp package ceiling: Proposal on table is 12% in exchange for 12-month commit + tighter SLA language. Can leadership approve up to 15% credit or do we want to push back? (Aditya/Rishi)
3) Legal priority: Rishi — can you triage the indemnity redline in renewal_redlines.docx ASAP? We need a counter by 5/28 to stay in sync with procurement timelines.
4) Technical remediation: Vivek — please prepare a short remediation plan (1-pager) and cost estimate for the latency fixes and a proposed QA/validation cadence.

Attachments: BrightWorks_QBR_deck_v3.pdf (working deck), renewal_redlines.docx, qbr_support_incident_log.csv

Why this is exec-level: BrightWorks has been a priority footprint for our public sector partner channel; losing or discounting aggressively sets an adverse precedent in the sector. We have room to negotiate product fixes + limited concession, but we need leadership calibration on permissible commercial moves and an approved legal position.

Thanks —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Thanks Naomi — good summary. Quick responses inline: 

- Exec attendance: I can take the QBR on 2027-06-02 but would prefer Laura to lead if she can (she's better for commercial discussion). If Laura is tied up, I’ll cover both product and ops.
- Credit ceiling: +1 to keeping commercial concessions to a max of 12% if we get a firm 12-month commit, otherwise we should not exceed 10%. Aditya/Rishi — this is an inbound ask from procurement; recommend we prepare a two-tier offer (standard vs. escalated) to keep flexibility.
- Legal: Rishi — this is high priority. The indemnity language is broader than typical for our standard term sheet; need narrow carveouts.
- Remediation plan: I’ll draft a one-pager by EOD Wed that outlines 1) perf patch ETA (Q2 rollback + hotfix), 2) test plan (production canary + synthetic workload run), and 3) estimated engineering hours and cost bucket.

Note on customer communication: If we commit to credits, we should couple credit with a technical remediation SLA and a pre-agreed post-deployment QA gate. Otherwise the discount looks like a stand-alone concession.

Vivek
VP, Product & Operations
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
From: Rachel Liu <rachel.liu@brightworks.com>

Subject: Re: QBR prep: BrightWorks account health & renewal risk register — exec attention

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the transparency and the deck. A few clarifications from our side before the QBR: 

- Latency: The biggest blocker for us is tail latency on long-context summarization; we see occasional 2-3x spikes relative to baseline during business hours. We need a plan that includes a mitigation ETA and a post-fix validation window.
- Credits: Procurement would like the 20% figure as an opening ask; we can settle in the 10-15% range with performance guarantees.
- Legal: I’ve looped our renewals team so we can get ahead on redlines. We prefer a bilateral indemnity approach to keep the contract symmetric.

We’re available for the proposed 2027-06-02 10:00 PDT. Can you send a finalized agenda and attendee list? Also — can you include a short summary (1 slide) showing before/after perf metrics and the proposed validation steps?

Best,
Rachel Liu
Head of Platform Ops — BrightWorks

1) QBR attendance (2027-06-02 10:00 PDT): Laura will lead commercial; Vivek will present the remediation plan and perf validation. Naomi and Aditya will cover renewal commercial framing.
2) Credit posture: Leadership preference is to start with a two-tiered offer: 10% standard (30-day remediation commit) vs. up-to-15% escalated (12-month commit + stricter SLA + post-implementation QA). Aditya — draft the two-tier offer language and send to Rishi for final legal vet.
3) Legal redlines: Rishi to produce counter-indemnity language by 5/28 COB.
4) Remediation doc: Vivek to deliver the 1-pager with ETA and test plan by 5/26 EOD.
5) Deck & agenda: I will refresh the QBR deck with a one-slide before/after perf plan and the incident timeline; final deck to external by 5/27 morning.

Action items with owners and deadlines are captured in the attached drive links. I’ll schedule a 30-minute dry run for internal alignment on 5/31 11:00 PDT — calendar invite to follow.
